q: Which city is home to this famous tower?
f: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.

q: What is this animal?
f: Wild giant pandas live in the mountains of central China.

q: Which planet is this?
f: Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice.

q: In which country are these pyramids?
f: The Great Pyramid of Giza is over 4,500 years old.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
f: Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and 2021.

q: How many players per team are on the court in basketball?
f: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith.

q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
f: The Pacific covers about one third of Earth's surface.

q: Which city is famous for this bridge?
f: The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.

q: How many continents are usually counted?
f: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air?
f: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar.

q: In which country is this ancient site?
f: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
f: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital, chosen in 1908.

q: What is the hardest natural material?
f: Diamond is pure carbon arranged in a crystal lattice.

q: Which is the longest river in Africa?
f: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

q: In which country is this monument?
f: The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife.

q: How many players does a soccer team have on the field?
f: That count includes the goalkeeper.

q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
f: Au comes from the Latin word aurum.

q: What is the fastest land animal?
f: A cheetah can reach around 100 km/h in short bursts.

q: In which country is this opera house?
f: The Sydney Opera House opened in 1973.

q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
f: More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

q: In which country is this ancient city?
f: Petra was carved into rock by the Nabataeans.

q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
f: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969.

q: What is the smallest country in the world?
f: Vatican City covers less than half a square kilometre.

q: In which country is this mountain?
f: Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
f: Ottawa sits on the border of Ontario and Quebec.

q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
f: Babies are born with around 300 bones that fuse over time.

q: Which country gave this statue to the United States?
f: The Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886.

q: Which element has the symbol Fe?
f: Fe comes from the Latin word ferrum.

q: In which city is this ancient arena?
f: The Colosseum was completed in 80 AD.

q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
f: The Sahara is about the size of the United States.

q: Which country has the most lakes?
f: Canada is home to more than half of the world's lakes.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
f: Ulaanbaatar is the coldest national capital in the world.

q: Which planet rotates on its side?
f: Uranus is tilted by about 98 degrees.

q: In which country is this temple?
f: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.

q: Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
f: Flying squirrels and sugar gliders only glide.

q: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games?
f: They were held in Athens in 1896, in this stadium.

q: Which language has the most native speakers?
f: Close to a billion people speak Mandarin as a first language.

q: What is the deepest lake in the world?
f: Lake Baikal in Siberia is over 1,600 metres deep.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
f: Wellington is the southernmost capital of a sovereign state.

q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
f: Light travels about 150 million km in roughly 8 min 20 s.
